_about: The Lens toolkit's building blocks (window.Lens, toolkit version 2). One entry per component — the AI reads this to choose and use them; a test checks it matches the toolkit exactly. Load the toolkit in a Lens with <script src="/lens-kit/lens-kit.js"></script>. Data always comes from window.lensBridge.call('execMDX', { mdx }) and is turned into rows with Lens.rows(result).

helpers.Lens.rows(cellset): Turn an execMDX result into tidy rows: one object per row tuple with _label, _members, one property per row dimension (its member name), and one property per column labelled by its member names joined with ' / '. Missing cells are null.
helpers.Lens.theme.colors: The shared palette (light/dark): ink, soft, faint, rule, panel, bg, accent, compare, good, bad, amber, series[].
helpers.Security: Every query runs as the signed-in user, so TM1 security may hide members or refuse a cube. Never hard-code a top member such as 'Total Company' — find the highest level the user can see (e.g. TM1FILTERBYLEVEL on levels 2, 1, 0 and take the first non-empty set). Treat attribute cubes (}ElementAttributes_<dim>) as optional: if reading captions fails, show element names instead of failing the whole Lens.
helpers.Alpine (CSP build): For simple interactivity (tabs, toggles). No inline code expressions: register behaviour with Alpine.data('name', () => ({ ... })) and reference it from x-data="name" and @click="methodName".

kpis.purpose: A row of headline figures, each compared with a target, forecast or prior year, with the variance coloured better/worse.
kpis.data: items: [{ label, value, compare?, format?, cost?, note?, compareLabel? }] — cost: true for expense lines (lower is better).
kpis.example: Lens.kpis('#kpis', [{ label: 'Revenue', value: 71566000, compare: 41583000, format: 'k$' }, { label: 'Operating expense', value: 13540000, compare: 4709000, format: 'k$', cost: true }], { compareLabel: 'Target' })

trend.purpose: A time series — bars or lines by period — optionally against a comparison line; bars turn red where they are worse than the comparison.
trend.data: categories: ['Jan', …]; series: [{ name, values: [n…], type: 'bar' | 'line', compare?: true }] — mark the comparison series with compare: true.

options.format: Number format for axis and tooltip.

trend.interactions: Hover tooltips; click a legend entry to hide a series.
trend.example: Lens.trend('#trend', { categories: ['Jan','Feb','Mar'], series: [{ name: 'Actual', values: [10,12,9] }, { name: 'Target', values: [11,11,11], compare: true }], format: 'k$' })

waterfall.purpose: A bridge from one total to another, step by step — what moved the result.
waterfall.data: steps: [{ label, value, total: true }, { label, value }, …, { label, value, total: true }] — first and last are totals; steps in between are signed changes (positive adds, negative takes away).
waterfall.example: Lens.waterfall('#bridge', { steps: [{ label: 'Target', value: 14094, total: true }, { label: 'Revenue', value: 29983 }, { label: 'Cost of sales', value: -21783 }, { label: 'Actual', value: 22294, total: true }], format: 'k$' })

bars.purpose: Horizontal bars by item (region, product, cost centre), each with a comparison marker and the variance; click a bar to drill in.
bars.data: rows: [{ key, label, value, compare? }] — key is passed to onClick (defaults to label).

options.onClick: function (key) — e.g. drill into that region.

bars.interactions: Hover tooltips; click a bar → onClick(key).
bars.example: Lens.bars('#regions', { rows: [{ key: '100', label: 'East Region', value: -1302, compare: 28 }], format: 'k$', onClick: k => drillInto(k) })

grid.purpose: A spreadsheet-style table — sorting, filtering, resizing, fast scrolling. Read-only in toolkit version 2 (editing comes with write-back).
grid.data: columns: [{ field, headerName, type?: 'number' | 'text', format? }]; rows: array of objects (e.g. from Lens.rows).

options.height: CSS height; defaults to fit the rows (max 480px).

grid.interactions: Click a header to sort; column filters; resize columns.
grid.example: Lens.grid('#tbl', { columns: [{ field: 'line', headerName: 'Line' }, { field: 'actual', headerName: 'Actual', type: 'number', format: 'k$' }], rows: [{ line: 'Payroll', actual: 7159000 }] })

flow.purpose: A network or tree with automatic layout — boxes and arrows you can zoom and drag.
flow.data: nodes: [{ id, label, sub?, kind?: 'root' | 'good' | 'bad' | 'neutral' }]; edges: [{ source, target, label? }].
flow.interactions: Zoom, pan, drag boxes; click a box → onClick(id).
flow.example: Lens.flow('#org', { nodes: [{ id: 'TC', label: 'Total Company', kind: 'root' }, { id: '100', label: 'East Region', kind: 'bad' }], edges: [{ source: 'TC', target: '100' }] })
